body:
Fixes #784

Router removes supported geolocation headers and structured search/retrieval location fields by default from routed HTTP and JSON WebSocket requests. Exactly one `x-router-share-geolocation: true` header opts in for that request or connection; Router consumes it. Account overrides cannot restore stripped metadata. Prompt content, user tool schemas and search availability retain their behavior.

Reproduce by routing a supported location header or structured search location without consent. Automated regressions cover default removal, explicit opt-in, duplicate/invalid consent, configured overrides, fragmented WebSocket forwarding and all eight independently mixed Gemini field spellings. Matching Rust regression source is included but remains unrun: every required JavaScript stage must pass for the same SHA before Rust starts.

This remains an authorized **draft CI feedback checkpoint**, with implementation and verification incomplete. Published checkpoint: `37147a95ce5fb1efeced23b2ba49dcd036a53a8a`. Freshly fetched main `eb2dad1c0a18394dc1aad46413e11401e74eb502` is included. The complete issue, required-sub-issue response and all three PR comment types were refreshed; no additional human requirement or required child issue was found.

The latest source batch counts complete private lexer storage from fixed record layouts under the original 200,000-cell bound. Exact-boundary and above-boundary regressions pass as complete files under Node and Bun, preserving hostile-input checks and mutable refusal copies. The actual compiler producer refreshes its complete registration and genuine portable Git objects. Full receiving attempts remain memory-interrupted. Earlier private-record and source-adoption allocation repairs retain every original workload and limit. These changes establish zero newly executable production functions. See the [cold storage repair](https://github.com/link-assistant/router/blob/issue-784-1f6838f56841/docs/case-studies/issue-784/current-static-cold-budget.md), [compiler registration](https://github.com/link-assistant/router/blob/issue-784-1f6838f56841/docs/case-studies/issue-784/current-static-cold-registration.md) and [original controller investigation](https://github.com/link-assistant/router/blob/issue-784-1f6838f56841/docs/case-studies/issue-784/current-allocation-controller-investigation.md).

The complete local gate on clean `f08eee0927b9f3b7c2081bf6d3d4fcf975adf644` completes five commands: asset/runner freshness, the complete lint implementation and runner controls. The original workflow tests start, then the unchanged cgroup guard interrupts the enclosing lint stage after 201.309 seconds at 2,867,679,232 sampled bytes. Native suites, TypeScript, parity and both translation cohorts are unrun at that SHA. Every owned process is reaped; no green stamp exists. Node 20.20.2, Bun 1.4.4 and lockfile-installed TypeScript 5.9.3 were used. Complete streams and receipts are retained in the [exact gate report](https://github.com/link-assistant/router/blob/issue-784-1f6838f56841/docs/case-studies/issue-784/current-f08eee-gate.md). Earlier passing stages remain evidence for their actual earlier heads. No original deadline, assertion, strictness or resource guard is relaxed; no local Rust tool ran.

The entire preceding `815527efb3db40ca7e650ba9aaae47bfa1529dab` cycle is terminal. [Run 42576266498](https://github.com/link-assistant/router/actions/runs/42576266498) has nine successful, 19 failed, six cancelled and 25 skipped jobs; all six supplemental workflows are terminal. All 25 nonpassing job logs and all 26 artifacts are preserved and verified. The independent audits contain **43 real original case deadline breaches**, separately from one intentional overdue negative control. Other failures include a missing owned-matrix TypeScript file, stale parity source hash, 271 stale and 54 missing canonical outputs, complete matrix cancellations, original semantic refusals and the private compiler's unchanged source-byte bound. See the [complete failure inventory and custody](https://github.com/link-assistant/router/blob/issue-784-1f6838f56841/docs/case-studies/issue-784/current-815527-ci-review.md).

The complete canonical draft verifies 2,873 nested outputs, 318,859,673 decoded output bytes and every declared published Git input. It measures 158 executable of 2,578 production top-level functions, with 2,420 carried. Four declared inputs changed in the local repair batch, so the preceding draft cannot be installed as current output. Strict parity remains unfinished: an earlier complete strict result has 441 fatal gaps (151 partial, 290 unsupported, two of 443 implemented features and 12,345 carried items); the latest strict job stops earlier at a stale source hash. Main's failures remain mandatory here. No missing-secret or human-only setup cause explains these code failures, and no manual action replaces their repair.

The literal guarantee that every tool never reveals any location also remains unmet: source-IP observation, provider security/account inference, direct telemetry or OAuth/MCP connections, and unsupported private client/subscription paths cannot be certified by Router's metadata filter. No vendor-account authorization/session was supplied for dashboard changes. The [case study](https://github.com/link-assistant/router/blob/issue-784-1f6838f56841/docs/case-studies/issue-784/README.md) inventories every requirement and source; the [configuration guide](https://github.com/link-assistant/router/blob/issue-784-1f6838f56841/docs/privacy/geolocation.md) explains supported behavior and limitations. The PR stays draft and unmerged until all required behavior and same-SHA checks are verified.
title: Default routed geolocation sharing to explicit per-request consent
